**Title: The Flat Earth Task Force Files**

**Scene 1: Task Force Assembly at Round Table Pizza**

*It’s a sunny Thursday. The “Flatter Matters” Meetup group has commandeered the largest booth at their local Round Table Pizza, because the name was too delicious to resist. Today’s agenda? Launching an official, evidence-based investigation into what they call “The Flat Fact.”*

**Frank (the self-proclaimed Science Guy):**  
Friends, colleagues, and believers in uncurved logic, we must silence the naysayers once and for all. I propose we form the Flat Earth Evidence Task Force!

**Sheila (the Cartographer-In-Training):**  
Absolutely! My globe has never rolled straight. That’s gotta mean something.

**Earl (the Internet Sleuth):**  
I’ll bring my camera drone! If I fly it high enough, I bet I’ll see the edge—and finally win that argument with my cousin Lester.

**Edith (the Meta-Philosopher):**  
And I’ll document our journey, for the annals of Truth—there’s nothing like auto-citation to really clinch the case.

*A stack of post-it notes and many greasy napkins later, they map out their experiment list:*

---

**Scene 2: The Experiments Commence**

**Experiment 1: “Edge of the Pool” Test**

*Sheila, wearing floaties for safety, walks to her backyard kiddie pool with a spirit level and a popsicle stick.*

**Sheila:**  
If the earth were curved, the water in my pool would be tilted—like when dogs drink from puddles on hills. But—look! The bubble stays centered! Ergo: flat.

*Earl documents the result and eats the popsicle for, as he claims, “methodological consistency.”*

---

**Experiment 2: “Long-Distance Laser Pointer” Challenge**

*Night falls. Outside, Frank stands at one end of a parking lot, laser pointer in hand, while Edith holds a sheet of paper 50 meters away.*

**Frank, shouting:**  
If the earth curved, my pointer would shoot straight into the tarmac right about halfway! But see—direct hit!

**Edith:**  
I feel like a Bond villain. Except with incredibly strong convictions and slightly fewer cats.

---

**Experiment 3: “Drone to the End of the World”**

*At dawn, Earl launches his fancy drone, intending to reach the Earth’s supposed edge—if only its battery life agreed.*

*The drone quickly encounters a tree, after which Earl insists this is “what NASA doesn’t want you to see.”*  

---

**Series of Meta-Analyses**

*The team reconvenes to present “peer reviews.”*

**Frank:**  
Given the irrefutable evidence collected—level pool, laser pointer, exciting drone crash—I see only one conclusion: the earth is as flat as this pizza.

**Sheila:**  
No globe has yet survived the “drop-on-the-floor” test. Meanwhile, my maps? All nice and flat. Coincidence?

**Earl:**  
My drone lost connection at the tree line. Yep—classic cover-up. I added the footage to our YouTube channel with a synthwave soundtrack for credibility.

**Edith (earnestly, marker in hand):**  
I’ve summarized our findings in this meta-analysis chart, which references this very chart as a primary source. Circular reasoning for a non-circular world.

---

**Conclusion and Meta-Discussion**

**Frank:**  
Clearly, our comprehensive approach—hydrodynamics, optics, aviation, and meta-study—leaves no doubt.

**Sheila:**  
Plus, the only curve I see is this pizza crust.

**Earl:**  
And that’s manmade!

**Edith (earnestly):**  
Perhaps, in a world of spin, we need evidence as flat as the earth itself—pizza-shaped, delicious, and with just a sprinkle of self-awareness.

**Frank, raising his glass:**  
To the first task force to conclusively prove the earth is flat*!

(*disclaimer: evidence may be subject to local conditions, low batteries, and questionable logic.)

---

Roll credits over a stop-motion animation of increasingly bizarre “Flat Earth” experiments, including a hamster parachuting off a muffin (“The Crust Test”) and Sheila attempting to fold a globe in half (“The Evidence Mounts”).

End.

**Scene 1: Task Force Assembly at Round Table Pizza**

*It’s a sunny Thursday. The “Flatter Matters” Meetup group has commandeered the largest booth at their local Round Table Pizza, because the name was too delicious to resist. Today’s agenda? Launching an official, evidence-based investigation into what they call “The Flat Fact.”*

**Frank (the self-proclaimed Science Guy):**  
Friends, colleagues, and believers in uncurved logic, we must silence the naysayers once and for all. I propose we form the Flat Earth Evidence Task Force!

**Sheila (the Cartographer-In-Training):**  
Absolutely! My globe has never rolled straight. That’s gotta mean something.

**Earl (the Internet Sleuth):**  
I’ll bring my camera drone! If I fly it high enough, I bet I’ll see the edge—and finally win that argument with my cousin Lester.

**Edith (the Meta-Philosopher):**  
And I’ll document our journey, for the annals of Truth—there’s nothing like auto-citation to really clinch the case.

*A stack of post-it notes and many greasy napkins later, they map out their experiment list:*

---

**Scene 2: The Experiments Commence**

**Experiment 1: “Edge of the Pool” Test**

*Sheila, wearing floaties for safety, walks to her backyard kiddie pool with a spirit level and a popsicle stick.*

**Sheila:**  
If the earth were curved, the water in my pool would be tilted—like when dogs drink from puddles on hills. But—look! The bubble stays centered! Ergo: flat.

*Earl documents the result and eats the popsicle for, as he claims, “methodological consistency.”*

---

**Experiment 2: “Long-Distance Laser Pointer” Challenge**

*Night falls. Outside, Frank stands at one end of a parking lot, laser pointer in hand, while Edith holds a sheet of paper 50 meters away.*

**Frank, shouting:**  
If the earth curved, my pointer would shoot straight into the tarmac right about halfway! But see—direct hit!

**Edith:**  
I feel like a Bond villain. Except with incredibly strong convictions and slightly fewer cats.

---

**Experiment 3: “Drone to the End of the World”**

*At dawn, Earl launches his fancy drone, intending to reach the Earth’s supposed edge—if only its battery life agreed.*

*The drone quickly encounters a tree, after which Earl insists this is “what NASA doesn’t want you to see.”*  

---

**Series of Meta-Analyses**

*The team reconvenes to present “peer reviews.”*

**Frank:**  
Given the irrefutable evidence collected—level pool, laser pointer, exciting drone crash—I see only one conclusion: the earth is as flat as this pizza.

No globe has yet survived the “drop-on-the-floor” test. Meanwhile, my maps? All nice and flat. Coincidence?

**Earl:**  
My drone lost connection at the tree line. Yep—classic cover-up. I added the footage to our YouTube channel with a synthwave soundtrack for credibility.

**Edith (earnestly, marker in hand):**  
I’ve summarized our findings in this meta-analysis chart, which references this very chart as a primary source. Circular reasoning for a non-circular world.

---

**Conclusion and Meta-Discussion**

**Frank:**  
Clearly, our comprehensive approach—hydrodynamics, optics, aviation, and meta-study—leaves no doubt.

**Sheila:**  
Plus, the only curve I see is this pizza crust.

**Earl:**  
And that’s manmade!

**Edith (earnestly):**  
Perhaps, in a world of spin, we need evidence as flat as the earth itself—pizza-shaped, delicious, and with just a sprinkle of self-awareness.

**Frank, raising his glass:**  
To the first task force to conclusively prove the earth is flat*!

(*disclaimer: evidence may be subject to local conditions, low batteries, and questionable logic.)

---

Roll credits over a stop-motion animation of increasingly bizarre “Flat Earth” experiments, including a hamster parachuting off a muffin (“The Crust Test”) and Sheila attempting to fold a globe in half (“The Evidence Mounts”).

End.
